title: Bug: [wr_arp] The test case arp/test_wr_arp.py::test_wr_arp is not aligned with change in ferret.py(PR#15835)
author: congh-nvidia
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

There is a change in the tests/arp/files/ferret.py made by PR#15835.
It changed the padding bytes in the payload of the arp packets:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/15835/files#diff-51cd7fcc6e0d30d81b0254bafba60849e0e26e9f308e5779d1f57f3d46a279beR177

But the test arp/test_wr_arp.py::test_wr_arp is not aligned with this change, the arp packets sent by the ferret will not match the expected packet in the test.
This happens in testPort function of ansible/rolse/test/files/ptftests/py3/wr_arp.py when comparing with count_matched_packets.

This causes failure like this:

### Steps to Reproduce

Run the test arp/test_wr_arp.py::test_wr_arp on any platforms.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

In KVM environments, it's possible that an ARP response that gets forwarded is less than 60 bytes, less than the minimum Ethernet frame size. In physical environments, it'll almost always be at least the minimum Ethernet frame size. In the lab, the `arp_responder.py` script adds a marker in the padding at the end of the ARP packet to indicate that it came from that script.

#### How did you do it?

To gracefully handle all cases, generate the expected ARP response packet as a 42-byte packet, and ignore extra bytes.

comments.body: Could you help me understand why the test starts failing on physical testbed as well? Is there any recent change in arp_responder?

comments.author: justin-wong-ce
comments.body:
> Could you help me understand why the test starts failing on physical testbed as well? Is there any recent change in arp_responder?

There was a recent change that changes the last 18 bytes of the responding arp packet from the ferret server.
This causes packet mismatches in the PTF test when checking the full default length of 60 bytes.

 https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/commit/8ea0d3e0f65bf0fd2ce8ce18dfe8deccfa68986b#diff-51cd7fcc6e0d30d81b0254bafba60849e0e26e9f308e5779d1f57f3d46a279beR177

Truncating the check to only 42 bytes (removing 18 bytes) would account for the recent 18 byte change in the return packet.
